description:
Split out of op-4daf when that bead's root-cause work closed (GitHub issue #28, 2026-08-21). Two residual items, neither blocking:

1. PER-ATOM-TYPE DEBYE-WALLER. After the evaluation's basis error is accounted for, ~1% of the SiC coherent-elastic residual remains, and it sits entirely in the weak |b_Si - b_C|^2 difference reflections (all-even hkl, h+k+l = 2 mod 4): +6.1% at n=20 rising monotonically to +23.5% at n=100. Growth with tau^2 confined to the difference reflections is the signature of a per-atom-type Debye-Waller factor inside the structure factor, F = sum_j b_j exp(-W_j tau^2) exp(i tau . r_j) -- Zhu 2014's 'exact Debye-Waller' option (card-5 iel=2 in the modified LEAPR) -- against the single compound coefficient this crate uses (Zhu's cubic approximation, iel=1, crystals::debye_waller_decks). Implementing the exact option would let the crate reproduce those reflections. Low value on its own since they are weak at the thermal point.

Related: the DW coefficients themselves differ, 4W' = 5.977/eV (tape, 300 K) vs 5.382/eV (this crate, 296 K), ~10% apart after temperature scaling. Not root-caused.

2. LITERATURE GAP. Zhu, Y. and Hawari, A. I. (2015), 'Implementation of a Generalized Coherent Elastic Scattering Formulation for Thermal Neutron Scattering Analysis', ICNC 2015, OSTI 23100909 -- the paper describing the in-house routine that actually produced the published MF=7/MT=2 (per reference-data/endf/tsl-SiinSiC.readme). No freely available copy located; NOT catalogued in kovan-literature. It is the document that would confirm or refute the basis finding in op-4daf. The 2014 MS thesis (the primary source actually used) IS catalogued: crates/kovan-literature/open/theses/zhu2014thermal.{json,pdf}.

See crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/docs/leapr-sic-coherent-elastic-vv.md.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
ITEM 1 DONE 2026-08-21, commit 26395482. Per-atom-type Debye-Waller (Zhu's 'exact' option) implemented and measured; the shape argument that predicted it is confirmed.

MEASURED. Residual against the published tape, per difference reflection (all-even hkl, h+k+l = 2 mod 4):
  n     compound      per-atom
  4      +2.8 %        +2.0 %
  12     +4.8 %        +2.0 %
  20     +6.9 %        +1.9 %
  36    +11.1 %        +1.9 %
  44    +13.4 %        +1.9 %
  52    +15.7 %        +1.9 %
Compound residual grows 5.6x across the range; per-atom is FLAT to within 0.1 percentage point. The tau-dependent component is therefore fully accounted for.

THE HEADLINE NUMBER DID NOT IMPROVE. sigma(0.0253 eV) 2.85303 b (-2.98 %) -> 2.84387 b (-3.30 %) vs the tape's 2.94078 b. Expected: the difference reflections are weak, so the total is dominated by sum reflections and by the basis question this option does not touch. An assertion pins that so it cannot be misread later as an improvement. The option is opt-in (ElasticChannel::GenerateExactDebyeWaller), never the default, and reports NotValidatedAgainstReferenceTape.

NEW LEAD, AND IT IS ON OUR SIDE. The flat ~2 % offset that remains matches in size and sign the ~10 % difference in the fitted W' itself: 5.977 /eV (tape, 300 K) vs 5.382 /eV (this crate, 296 K) after temperature scaling. Unlike the basis question this is about THIS PORT, needs no outside expertise, and is the most likely place a real defect on our side is still hiding. That is now this bead's remaining technical work, alongside item 2.

IMPLEMENTATION. coher::general::coher_general_with_per_atom_debye_waller folds exp(-2 W'_j E_tau) into each atom's amplitude, shared inner sum keeps the compound path byte-identical, wrong-length slice falls back rather than misassigning. endout::ElasticOutput::CoherentPreWeighted stops the factor being applied twice -- added as an enum variant not a flag so the decision had to be made at every match site, which immediately caught a second dispatch site in the validation reporter. crystals::debye_waller_deck_for_species gives the per-species decomposition with a test that it and the compound deck list name the same set.

Two of the new tests initially failed on MY wrong expectations, not the code: W' set to 0.05 /eV where SiC's real value is ~1.35 /eV; and the synthetic final edge treated as a reflection when it is a duplicated histogram-extension edge (the two paths weight it differently by 3.0e-4, now excluded and documented rather than papered over).

ITEM 2 (locate Zhu & Hawari ICNC 2015) still open.

Verified: njoy capped suite 626 passed / 0 failed / 8 ignored (exit 0, was 621); outram-mc-libs TRISO 4 passed / 1 ignored; cargo check --workspace --lib --tests clean. Rebased onto three tampines-steam-tables-gui commits, no conflicts. Pushed to develop. GitHub issue #28 updated and stays open.

title: njoy: SiC coherent elastic -- per-atom-type Debye-Waller (Zhu 'exact' option) + locate Zhu & Hawari ICNC 2015

description:
Split from op-9c2e (GitHub issue #30 body, point 3: 'themeing same as tampines-steam-tables'). kovan-gui currently applies zero theme (eframe::NativeOptions::default()).

SCOPE: port a GuiTheme-equivalent to kovan's GUI, matching crates/tampines-steam-tables/examples/tampines-steam-tables-gui/theme.rs's Gruvbox Dark / Gruvbox Light palette and apply() mechanics.

PROVENANCE (carry forward, don't re-derive): the tampines theme.rs already documents the Gruvbox palette as based on morhetz/gruvbox (https://github.com/morhetz/gruvbox), MIT licensed, with the attribution written into that file's own header. Any copy of the palette values into kovan must carry the same attribution -- see the workspace CLAUDE.md README-provenance conventions and that file's own header comment for the exact wording to mirror.

REUSE VS DUPLICATE: theme.rs lives in an EXAMPLE binary of tampines-steam-tables (crates/tampines-steam-tables/examples/tampines-steam-tables-gui/), not the library, so it is not import-able as a dependency from crates/kovan the way a library module would be. Decide at implementation time whether to (a) duplicate the palette constants with attribution (cheapest, matches this workspace's own precedent for GUI-example reference data -- see tampines-steam-tables-gui/reference_data/mod.rs's documented reasoning for why some of its own data is duplicated rather than imported), or (b) extract a small shared theme crate/module both GUIs depend on. Not a hard call either way -- note the choice made when this is picked up.
